title: Fastpath Integration Snippets & Sandbox Notebook (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This notebook collects the smallest, most repeatable SDK integration snippets and a lightweight sandbox protocol for internal teams to validate an initial integration within 20–30 minutes. Goal: give a developer a minimal success path, a few common failure modes and recovery steps, plus a tiny incident sandbox they can run locally to reproduce common errors (auth, timeout, streaming reconnect).

Why this exists (pain we see):
- New integrators leave after first failure: opaque error messages, token/cost surprises, streaming gaps.
- Large playbooks are ignored; we need an ultra-compact set that proves value fast.

Quick success path (0–30 min):
1) Create API key: console -> API keys -> "dev-temp" -> copy token
2) Minimal hello: curl sample to verify auth + reachability (30s)
   - curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","prompt":"Say hi"}'
3) SDK check (2–3 lines): pick language, run example
   - Python: pip install redwood-sdk
     from redwood import RedwoodClient
     c = RedwoodClient(api_key="$TOKEN")
     print(c.generate("Hello from local"))
4) Validate streaming: run stream example, confirm chunked output within 200–400ms per chunk
5) Embed + search quick sanity: compute embedding then query with cosine similarity

Core snippets (copyable):
- Auth failing (401): verify token length and source, check console rate-limits, check clock skew on VM
- Timeout default: client default=60s; for interactive UIs use 8s for first chunk, 30s for completion
- Reconnect strategy for streaming: exponential backoff 200ms -> 800ms -> 2s, resume from last token index

Tiny incident sandbox (local reproducible):
- Requirements: docker (optional), python 3.10+, local env var REDWOOD_API_KEY
- Steps:
  1) Start: python sandbox/serve_stub.py (runs a tiny HTTP stub that simulates slow token emission and occasional 500s)
  2) Run: python sandbox/client_probe.py --concurrency 5 --pattern slow-first-chunk
  3) Observe logs: each simulated 500 should trigger fallback to non-streaming path and a metric increment
- Files included: serve_stub.py (simple Flask app), client_probe.py (asyncio script that exercises SDK calls), sample-prompts.txt (edge-case prompts)

Integration checklist (pre-merge):
- [ ] Happy-path: generation returns 200 and content for short prompt
- [ ] Streaming: UI receives first chunk within SL0 (configurable per product)
- [ ] Fallback: simulated 500 triggers fallback policy and UX shows retry affordance
- [ ] Cost preview: tokens estimate returned and surfaced to product team
- [ ] Telemetry hooks: request_id, model, latency_ms, token_count logged to our tracing endpoint

Observability pointers for integrators: brief heuristics
- Tag requests with route_name and internal_user_id to allow per-route breakdowns in Console
- Surface request_id in UI error card (users can paste for support)
- Add histogram buckets at [5, 20, 50, 200, 1000] ms for first-chunk latency

Common decision notes (for product & SDK owners):
- Default retry count for ephemeral network errors: 2. Too many retries increase token cost and confusing duplicates.
- Streaming vs non-streaming default: enable streaming for interactivity-first surfaces; allow opt-out via a client flag.
- Local dev ergonomics: SDK should auto-fall back to a local emulator endpoint when REDWOOD_LOCAL_EMU=true to avoid accidental prod calls during demo.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want an official tiny npm package (redwood-mini) that wraps only auth + streaming reconnection? (pros: quick onboarding; cons: more surface area to maintain)
- Metric: what conversion metric proves fastpath value? Hypothesis: time-to-first-successful-call <= 10 minutes increases retention by 15%. Need AB test.
- Should the sandbox include synthetic cost burn to demo failing cost alerts? (low priority)

Appendix: quick debug commands
- Check token scopes: curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/whoami -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
- Replay request: save body.json then: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/replay -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @body.json (internal-only endpoint)
- Increase client debug: export REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug; SDK will print request_id and timing

Notes to self (messy brain dump):
- Keep snippets tiny. People copy/paste; make sure examples are actually runnable without additional deps.
- Consider adding a "cheat sheet" card in Console that exposes the 5 one-liners from this doc.
- Walk through this with Solutions Eng next week; get 3 quick wins to include in demo kit.

End of draft.
